is the only non-linear step in the whole layer, and Section B measures what it does to the hidden units.

. Each hidden unit is a weighted sum of all

. It looks trivial, but the model
would be two linear maps, and two linear maps in a row are just one

is also what makes each word use a
different part of the block, because which units survive depends on the word’s own numbers: "dog" and "sat" switch off
of those are the same. Section B counts the switched-off units for every word.
bends smoothly through zero instead of snapping: a small negative
input gives a small negative output and a real gradient, so the unit can
agree far from zero and disagree near it. The table puts the same inputs z through both. For a
large positive z both give back z; for a large negative z both give (almost)
× Φ(z), where Φ(z) is the chance that a random number from a standard bell curve
is smaller than z — so each value is kept in proportion to how "surely positive" it looks.

text.tspan: of the block’s output numbers, and the result is ADDED to x — the x
. Nothing normalises the sum, just like after attention in
: that is pre-norm. This is the end of one
encoder layer: the next layer receives this tensor and runs attention on it all over again. The two halves need each other —
attention moves information BETWEEN words, this block transforms it WITHIN each word. A stack of attention alone would
only ever produce averages; a stack of feed-forward blocks alone would never let two words meet.
